commits.message:
fix(parsing): stop splitting a single posting into two records on a restated job title

Bug report: "even though we have made many changes why are these email
parsing very low in quality... most of the messages are going in the
same way." Investigated the given message ID and found the root cause:
this vendor's template states the title once as a labeled field near
the top ("Job Title : QE Automation Engineer"), then restates the
exact same title a second time inside the "Job Description:" paragraph
itself ("Job Description:\n\nJob Title: QE Automation Engineer\n\nRole
Descriptions: We are seeking..."). _split_requirement_sections (app/
email_parsing/parsers.py) treated EVERY "Job Title:"/"Position:"/
"Role:" occurrence as a new record boundary, so this single posting
split into two "records": a near-empty stub ending right before the
repeated label (job_description == "...Exp: 8+ years\n\nJob
Description:", 109 characters), and the real 4,000-character content
with the actual required skills starting there. Since the review UI
only ever renders the FIRST record (frontend/src/pages/
DraftDetailPage.tsx and components/DraftTypeLabel.tsx both hardcode
records[0]), the entire real posting was completely invisible to the
reviewer behind what looked like an empty draft -- and this vendor
template shape (state the title, then restate it inside the JD body)
turns out to be extremely common across postings, matching "most of
the messages" in the report.

Fixed by collapsing a "Job Title:"/"Position:"/"Role:" match into the
previous one when its own labeled value is the SAME title (case/
whitespace-insensitive) -- a genuine second position always states a
DIFFERENT title, so real multi-position emails (both the numbered-list
shape and the label-based shape) still split correctly; verified with
a new test alongside the fix.

Directly analyzed the effect on the current backlog before writing the
fix: of 7,217 pending job-requirement drafts, 106 had record_count > 1
(this exact failure mode) and 507 had a job_description under 150
characters in the visible first record (this failure mode plus the
relay-masthead truncation fixed earlier). Backfilling those existing
drafts with the fixed parser is a separate follow-up step, not part of
this commit (re-running the LLM fallback across hundreds of drafts has
a real cost and should be scoped and confirmed on its own).

New coverage in scripts/hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py: the exact
QE Automation Engineer email from production now produces one record
with the full description and real skills (Selenium, Cucumber, Java,
JUnit, TestNG, Maven, Git, Jenkins) recovered; a companion test
confirms two genuinely different "Job Title:"-labeled positions still
split into two records, guarding against the fix over-merging a real
multi-position email. Full regression suite run against a fresh schema
and freshly built image: hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py (the script
covering this change) passes all checks including the 2 new ones, and
the existing numbered-multi-position and label-based-multi-position
regression tests continue to pass unchanged; every other failure in
the suite reproduces identically against the current, unmodified
production image in the same throwaway harness (missing live server,
missing Langfuse/MS Graph credentials) -- confirmed pre-existing
environment gaps, not regressions from this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
